title: Concurrent session refresh causing transient privilege downgrades across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Multiple customers (hosted and Dedicated) reported intermittent 403s following API key rotation and high-concurrency workloads. Investigation shows a race between the token refresh flow and API-key/organization-scoping updates which transiently produced tokens with reduced scopes (privilege downgrades). This affected Hosted API users, Dedicated clusters with ours-managed refresh proxies, and a Private VPC deployment where an out-of-sync Redis replica amplified the window of inconsistency.
steps_to_repro: 1) Create user+API key, 2) Start sustained parallel requests (200 rps) that rely on cached bearer tokens, 3) Rotate the API key and simultaneously trigger programmatic refresh for affected sessions, 4) Observe 403s for a subset of requests and tokens that previously had broader org scope being accepted only for narrower scopes.
root_cause: Token refresh path is not atomic with API-key metadata updates. The refresh flow checks cached token validity and then issues a new token based on the metadata snapshot. If the key rotation/update arrives between cache check and token issue, the issued token can be created against partial metadata (old org-scoping flags missing), producing tokens with stale or narrow privileges. In Private deployments using Redis replication lag, the service that constructs token claims read inconsistent key metadata from a lagging replica. Additionally, concurrent workers use an in-memory optimistic cache without proper CAS semantics, allowing two refreshes to race and one to commit a narrower scope.
mitigation: Applied an emergency server-side mitigation: added a temporary gating layer that rejects refresh requests if key rotation was visible within the last 30s and forces a full metadata re-sync. For Private customer X we disabled the read-replica fallback for auth metadata and forced reads from primary until a patch deploy. We notified impacted customers and applied request-level retries with backoff on our SDKs as a temporary workaround.
fix_plan: 1) Introduce atomic token refresh operation that snapshots key+org metadata under a short-lived lock (via Redis SETNX CAS) before issuing new tokens
2) Add versioned key metadata: issue refresh tokens only when client presents latest key metadata version or include metadata_version in token claims
3) Remove in-memory optimistic write path; route refresh commits through centralized token service with CAS semantics
4) For Private deployments, add healthcheck/lag-detection for metadata read replicas and avoid stale reads for auth flows
5) Create integration tests simulating concurrent rotation+refresh under high QPS and verify no scope regressions
6) Roll out fix as Canary -> 50% -> 100% with feature flag and metrics gating
rollout_plan: Canary in Hosted for low-latency customers (5%) for 8 hours with active monitoring on auth-errors and token-scope-discrepancies. If stable, increase to 50% for 24 hours, then full rollout. For Dedicated customers schedule maintenance window with opt-in and pre-checks. For Private customers provide signed patch and runbook; for air-gapped installs coordinate with SOC for KMS/HSM key sync.
monitoring_and_alerts: Added alert: spike in auth.errors with tag=scope_mismatch > 5 per min
Dashboard: Token refresh timeline vs key-rotation events
